Software engineer with over 5 years of experience developing and maintaining internal web-based development tools, including frontend, backend, and automation infrastructure at Intel. projects.title: Breast Cancer Classification with SVM
projects.description:
This project utilizes supervised machine learning (support vector machine) for breast cancer classification.

Support vector machines (SVMs) are memory efficient and can assist with early diagnosis and prediction automation of cancer. Training data was obtained from the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) data set, which is used to diagnose tumor scans as benign or cancerous; using images of biopsies.

The predictions of the trained model currently have accuracy of +96%.

projects.title: Improve Industrial Hemp Cultivation with a Smart IoT Soil Spectroscopy System
projects.description:
Engineered a low-cost system (>500 USD) to assist farmers with agricultural techniques for industrial hemp cultivation, which utilizes artificial intelligence for soil analysis, to determine soil quality.

Hemp has been cultivated since 2700 BC for its various beneficial qualities, however the current total supply does not meet global demands. Soil quality is crucial in influencing the overall quality of harvest of industrial hemp. Specific soil properties such as pH, organic matter, and nitrogen must be taken into consideration. While there are numerous laboratory tests available to evaluate soil composition, none are particularly cost-effective. Other portable spectrometers that also display nutrient results in real-time cost on average $4,000 USD or higher.

Soil spectroscopy is the identification and analysis of the interaction of visible nearinfrared (vis-NIR) wavelengths with soil properties, and is an environmentally-friendly, fast, nondestructive, and reproducible alternative to traditional laboratory analyses. 

This smart IoT soil spectroscopy system allows for farmers to determine if soil is favorable for industrial hemp production, at a low cost.

Hardware used: 
- Raspberry Pi 4: main controller
- Arduino UNO: data collection via serial communication
- Touchscreen display: easy user interaction for onsite testing
- Spectral sensor: scan soil and collect reflectance values at various wavelengths

Software used:
- Tkinter: graphical user interface
- Pandas, NumPy and Scikit-Learn: data collection and analysis

Programming languages: Python, C++
